abstract: Cutler, Pebody and Sarkar introduced a fractional size $\lVert\gamma\rVert$ for finitely supported weights on $\mathbb{Z}$ and showed that if $A_n\subset\mathbb{Z}^n$ includes each point independently with probability $\prod_i\alpha(x_i)$, for a fractional set $\alpha\colon\mathbb{Z}\to[0,1]$ of total mass $a>1$, then $\mathbb{E}|A_n+kA_n|$ grows at the exponential rate $\lVert\alpha+k\alpha\rVert$ for fixed nonzero $k$. They conjectured that the random cardinality itself has this rate, and proved it only in a strictly spartan regime. For every such $\alpha$ and every fixed nonzero integer $k$ we prove $\operatorname{Var}|A_n+kA_n|\leq4(a^n+2)\,\mathbb{E}|A_n+kA_n|$ and $\lVert\alpha+k\alpha\rVert>a$; hence $|A_n+kA_n|/\mathbb{E}|A_n+kA_n|\to1$ almost surely and in $L^2$, with exponentially small probability of any fixed relative deviation, and $\frac1n\log|A_n+kA_n|\to\log\lVert\alpha+k\alpha\rVert$ almost surely, with no spartan assumption. The variance bound is a direct deletion-counting argument combined with the Efron–Stein inequality and a covariance identity for Bernoulli coordinates. An explicit example has its minimizing exponent strictly inside $(0,1)$, and for every non-singleton fractional set of mass one the empty-set probability tends to $e^{-1}$, showing that $a>1$ is needed. Consequences: a single sequence of finite integer sets realizes the fractional dilate exponents for every fixed nonzero $k$, and the closures of finite-set and fractional-set nonzero-dilate profiles coincide. We also note that the simultaneous-realization conjecture as printed fails at $k=0$, and that the fractional version of the question $|A||A+2A|\leq|A+A|^2$ fails below mass one and is equivalent to the finite question above mass one. Limitations: only fractional sets (weights at most one) and nonzero dilates are covered; the expectation asymptotics are imported from Cutler–Pebody–Sarkar; the profile regions themselves are not determined. Small exact rational checks are supplied in the supplement.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Resolved both minor clarifications noted in the v2 review: (i) defined the deletion loss D_x = Z(A) - Z(A \ {x}) for every x in X (so D_x = 0 when x is not in A and D_x = X_x Delta_x globally on {0,1}^X), sharpened the deletion bound for x in A to D_x <= |(x+kA) union (A+kx)| <= 2|A| - 1 <= 2|A| via the common diagonal element (1+k)x, and included a one-sentence inline proof of the Efron-Stein inequality via orthogonal martingale differences; and (ii) clarified in Theorem 1 that n_0 = n_0(alpha, k, varepsilon, c) depends qualitatively on (alpha, k, varepsilon, c) via [1, Theorem 4], whereas the threshold log(b/a) for admissible exponential rates c in (0, log(b/a)) is independent of varepsilon.
- Added explicit theorem, lemma, corollary, and proposition locators for the primary-source references in the Problem and contribution and Related work sections ([1, Theorems 4, 5, 24 and 37; Lemma 33], [3, Theorems 1.1, 3.1 and 3.3; Conjecture 4.2], [4, Theorems 1.1-1.3 and Corollary 8.1], [5, Theorems 1, 2 and 13], [6, Theorems 1.2, 1.5-1.9 and Corollary 1.4], [7, Theorems 1.1-1.5 and Propositions 7.3-7.4], [8, Theorem 2.4, Corollaries 3.1 and 4.5, Propositions 4.2, 5.1 and 6.4, and (6.18)]), contrasted Step 1's strict inequality ||alpha + k alpha|| > ||alpha|| with the non-strict inequality of [1, Lemma 33], added open-access arXiv identifiers to [3, 6, 7], and pinned [8]'s URL to v2.
- Extended Remark 3 from the single example alpha = (1/2) 1_{0,1} to every fractional set alpha of total mass a = 1: if |supp(alpha)| = 1 then Z_n = 1 deterministically, whereas for every alpha with a = 1 and |supp(alpha)| >= 2 we have P(Z_n = 0) = P(A_n = empty) = prod_{x in B^n} (1 - q_x) -> e^{-1}.
- Updated the author line to the standard affiliation format, renamed Reproducibility to Data availability, and upgraded supplement/check_lemmas.py, the supplement README, and supplement/CONTENTS.sha256: replaced all assert statements with explicit require() checks so python3 -O executes every check, added exact rational verification of global D_x = X_x Delta_x, D_x <= 2|A| - 1, the Step 1 proof inequalities (0 < gamma(t) <= a, sum_t gamma(t) = a^2 > a, |supp(gamma)| >= 2|B| - 1 > |B| >= a) on 246 random fractional sets, non-uniform mass-one empty-set convergence, and 4 fault-injection self-tests.
title: Concentration of Random Tensor Sumsets
